growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P2 as the current market condition; the company's own outlook notes that 'the eventual normalization of Persian Gulf trade therefore does not necessarily imply an immediate normalization of the tanker market' but this is a forward-looking judgment, not a guarantee.
growth_thesis.claim: The US-Iran conflict and the resulting disruption to Persian Gulf oil trade flows are the primary near-term driver of elevated product tanker freight rates, as shuttle tanker and ship-to-ship operations absorb substantial tanker capacity.
quotes: tanker freight markets were supported by continued disruptions to global oil trade flows stemming from the conflict involving the US and Iran

Following the collapse of the temporary ceasefire in July, increasing volumes of crude and refined products were exported from the Persian Gulf through shuttle tanker and ship-to-ship operations, creating significant logistical inefficiencies and absorbing substantial tanker capacity

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P2 as announced orders, exercised options, and secured options; delivery timing through 2030 is the company's own characterization.
growth_thesis.claim: TORM is growing its fleet through a pipeline of newbuildings (six MR newbuildings ordered, two MR options exercised, eight LR2 newbuildings via a 50/50 JV, and two further MR options secured) to renew and expand capacity through 2030.
quotes: Following the acquisition of six MR resale vessels during the second quarter and the previously announced order of six MR newbuildings during the third quarter, TORM exercised options for an additional two MR newbuildings. Subsequent to quarter-end, TORM entered into agreements for eight LR2 newbuildings to be held through a 50/50 joint venture structure, and secured options for an additional two MR newbuildings.

Collectively, these investments establish a significant pipeline of future fleet deliveries through 2030, reinforcing TORM's commitment to a modern and efficient fleet while supporting future earnings growth and long-term shareholder value creation.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P2 as actual Q3 2026 results and as guidance ranges; the 88% fixed coverage at USD/day 50,487 supports the lower bound but the open 12% is exposed to spot.
growth_thesis.claim: Fleet-wide TCE rates in Q3 2026 reached USD/day 40,102, up from USD/day 31,012 a year earlier, and the nine-month average was USD/day 44,803 versus USD/day 28,151 in the prior-year period, indicating a structurally higher earnings base in 2026.
quotes: TORM achieved fleet-wide TCE rates of USD/day 40,102 on average (2025, same period: USD/day 31,012)

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P2 as of a specific date (28 October 2026); the rates are contractual commitments already in place.
growth_thesis.claim: High forward coverage provides earnings visibility: as of 28 October 2026, 53% of Q4 2026 earning days were fixed at USD/day 78,419, and 88% of full-year 2026 earning days were fixed at USD/day 50,487.
quotes: As of 28 October 2026, TORM had covered 53% of the Q4 2026 earning days at an average rate of USD/day 78,419
For the full year 2026, 88% of the earning days have been fixed at an average rate of USD/day 50,487

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P2 as a market observation for Q3 2026; the 4% figure is the company's estimate of the capacity reduction.
growth_thesis.claim: Approximately two-thirds of the LR2 fleet trading in the dirty (crude) segment has reduced clean product tanker (CPP) carrying capacity by around 4% compared with the start of 2026, creating a structural supply-side constraint that supports LR2 product tanker earnings.
quotes: approximately two-thirds of the LR2 fleet continued to trade in the "dirty" segment during the third quarter. This effectively reduced CPP-carrying capacity by around 4% compared with the start of the year, adding another layer of supply-side tightness and supporting LR2 earnings at levels significantly above historical norms throughout the quarter.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P2 as the company's market outlook; the 50m barrel figure is cited as an EU action. The restocking demand is a forward-looking inference by the company, not a committed figure.
growth_thesis.claim: The release of strategic petroleum inventories (e.g., 50 million barrels of diesel by EU countries) and the subsequent need to replenish those inventories will create an additional, potentially sustained, source of tanker demand and ton-miles beyond the immediate conflict-driven disruption.
quotes: inventories released today will ultimately need to be replenished, creating incremental import requirements and tanker demand once market conditions allow

The resulting restocking cycle could provide a meaningful additional source of tanker demand and ton-miles, particularly if inventories are rebuilt beyond the levels prevailing before the Iran conflict.

TORM's net interest-bearing debt was USD 848.4m, and the net loan-to-value ratio was 29.4% (Tanker segment only).

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4 (12 October 2026) and P2 (Q3 results, November 2026) as the company's official guidance; the step-up from the October guidance to the November guidance is incremental and reflects Q3 actuals plus Q4 booking.
growth_thesis.claim: TORM raised its full-year 2026 TCE guidance to USD 1,750 - 1,900m and EBITDA guidance to USD 1,350 - 1,500m, reflecting the company's expectation that the strong market will persist through Q4 2026.
quotes: full-year 2026 TCE is now expected to be in the range of USD 1,750 - 1,900m, compared with USD 1,700 - 1,900m following the guidance upgrade announced on 12 October 2026. EBITDA is now expected to be in the range of USD 1,350 - 1,500m, compared with USD 1,300 - 1,500m previously.

TORM now expects full-year 2026 TCE to be in the range of USD 1,700 – 1,900m and full-year 2026 EBITDA to be in the range of USD 1,300 – 1,500m, compared to previous guidance of TCE of USD 1,400 – 1,600m and EBITDA of USD 1,000 – 1,200m.

risks.basis: Stated in P4 (cyclical nature in risk-factor text), F2 (three-year EBIT trend), and P2 (9M 2026 vs 2025 comparison and fleet renewal details).

quotes: the highly cyclical nature of the industry that we operate in
